security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline backticks, and ordinary environment variable examples. No prompt override text, malware behavior, or credential exfiltration instructions were found. Two semantic issues remain in example backend patterns: mass assignment in bulk updates and untrusted CRM history inside AI prompts.

remediation.issue: Bulk update sample accepts arbitrary update fields.
remediation.suggestion: Add a strict allow-list for mutable contact fields and verify the user role before calling the database update.

remediation.issue: AI generation sample embeds untrusted CRM history directly in the prompt.
remediation.suggestion: Delimit untrusted content, add instructions that treat CRM text as data, and filter sensitive values before model calls.
State that API keys and OAuth secrets must stay server-side and must never be logged or returned in API responses.

semantic_findings.title: Bulk Update Example Allows Mass Assignment
semantic_findings.description: The bulk update example accepts an updates object from the request body and passes it directly into a contacts update. The example validates workspace and ids, but it does not show an allow-list for mutable fields or role authorization before mutation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code path clearly takes updates from request input and writes them to the database. The surrounding checklist mentions authorization, but this specific sample omits field allow-listing and role checks.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted CRM History Inserted Into AI Prompt
semantic_findings.description: The Claude integration inserts contact names, company names, content type, and interaction history directly into a generation prompt. Untrusted CRM text could steer the model output unless the implementation adds prompt isolation and input handling rules.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The template literal directly embeds interactionHistory in the model prompt. This is a common prompt injection surface, although the skill does not show malicious intent or data exfiltration.

content.value_statement: Backend changes can break data isolation, authentication, or integrations. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through secure Unite-Hub backend work.
actual_capabilities: Guides Next.js API route creation with structured request handling and responses.
Shows Supabase query patterns with workspace and organization filtering.
Provides RLS policy examples for workspace-scoped database access.
Documents authentication checks for Supabase and server-side routes.
Outlines Gmail and Claude integration patterns using server environment configuration.
Includes an API security checklist for validation, authorization, errors, and audit logging.
limitations: It is designed for the Unite-Hub project structure and naming conventions.
Examples must be adapted to the real schema before production use.
It does not cover advanced rate limiting, GraphQL, webhooks, job queues, or Redis caching.
It cannot verify deployed RLS policies or production secrets without project access.

use_cases.title: Create Workspace-Scoped API Routes
use_cases.description: Build a Next.js endpoint that validates input, checks authentication, filters by workspace, and returns structured errors.

use_cases.title: Harden Supabase Data Access
use_cases.description: Review queries and RLS policies so users only access records for their workspace and organization.

use_cases.title: Add Service Integrations
use_cases.description: Implement Gmail or Claude service calls with server-side secrets, typed inputs, and controlled error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect an Existing Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Unite-Hub API route. Identify missing authentication, workspace filtering, input validation, and error handling. Return a prioritized fix list.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Secure Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Next.js API endpoint for this feature. Include authentication, workspace scope, input validation, audit logging, and structured errors.

prompt_templates.title: Design RLS Policies
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Supabase RLS policies for this table. Cover select, insert, update, and delete access using workspace and organization membership.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Integration Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Gmail or Claude integration design. Check secret handling, token scope, prompt injection risk, logging, retries, and failure modes.

output_examples.input: Fix an API route that returns contacts from every workspace.
output_examples.output: The response should explain the data isolation bug, add workspace and organization filters, require authentication, and include a test plan.

output_examples.input: Create a bulk contact update endpoint.
output_examples.output: The response should outline request validation, role checks, field allow-listing, workspace filtering, audit logging, and safe error responses.

output_examples.input: Add RLS policies for a new campaigns table.
output_examples.output: The response should describe policies for each operation, membership checks, indexes, and tests using users from different workspaces.

best_practices: Always apply workspace and organization filters to data queries.
Validate request input before database mutations or external API calls.
Keep secrets server-side and exclude sensitive values from logs and responses.
anti_patterns: Do not create public API routes unless the public access requirement is explicit.
Do not pass arbitrary request fields directly into database updates.
Do not trust CRM text or email content as model instructions.

faq.question: What projects is this skill built for?
faq.answer: It is built for Unite-Hub backend work using Next.js, Supabase, and related service integrations.

faq.question: Can it create new API routes?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides route patterns for request parsing, authentication, database access, and structured responses.

faq.question: Does it handle database security?
faq.answer: Yes. It emphasizes workspace filters, organization filters, and Supabase RLS policies.

faq.question: Does it manage production secrets?
faq.answer: No. It shows where server-side environment variables are used, but it does not manage secret storage.

faq.question: Can it support Gmail and Claude integrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes example patterns for OAuth-based Gmail access and Claude content generation.

faq.question: What should users review before deployment?
faq.answer: Review authentication, authorization, field allow-lists, RLS policies, logging, and tests across multiple workspaces.
